samples.text:
The diagram show how olive oil is produced. There are nine stages, from harvesting the olives to using the by-product.

First, olives are harvested between October and December. The olives are shaken from the trees and they fall onto a nets. Then the olives are washed for removing leaves and dirt. After that, the olives and the stones are crushed and they become a paste.

Next step is malaxation, the paste is stirred slowly for 30–40 minutes. Then a centrifuge separate the oil from water and solids. After this, the oil is left in steel tanks for 4–6 weeks to settle. Then it is filtered, so the particles which remain are removed. After filtering, the oil is sealed in dark glass bottles.

Finally, the pulp which is left over is dried and burned as a fuel. Overall, it is a linear process with many steps and some of them take long time, especially the settling in the tanks, and even the waste is used in the end.
samples.why: Basic overview given late · all nine stages covered but linking is repetitive (Then, After that) · adequate vocabulary · several article, agreement and preposition errors that never obscure meaning.

samples.text:
The diagram outlines the process by which olive oil is produced, from the harvest to the use of waste material.

Overall, there are nine stages in this linear process. The main product, bottled oil, is obtained at the eighth stage, while the final step involves making use of the leftover pulp. The time needed for the stages ranges from minutes to several weeks.

The process begins between October and December, when olives are shaken from the trees onto nets. They are then washed to remove leaves and dirt, before both the olives and their stones are ground into a paste. This paste undergoes malaxation, meaning it is slowly stirred for 30 to 40 minutes, after which a centrifuge is used to separate the oil from water and solids.

Following this, the oil is left to rest in steel tanks for between four and six weeks. Any remaining particles are then filtered out, and the oil is sealed in dark glass bottles. Finally, the leftover pulp is dried and burn as fuel, which means that very little is wasted.
samples.why: Clear overview of stages and outcome · logical sequencing with varied linkers · some less common vocabulary (undergoes, leftover pulp) · mostly error-free sentences with one verb form slip.

samples.text:
The diagram illustrates the sequence of steps involved in manufacturing olive oil, from gathering the fruit to disposing of the residue.

In total, the process comprises nine linear stages. It starts with the seasonal harvest and culminates in bottling, with a final step in which the waste pulp is recovered as a source of energy.

Harvesting takes place from October to December, when the olives are shaken from the trees and caught in nets. After being washed to clear away leaves and dirt, the fruit is crushed, stones included, into a paste. This paste is then subjected to malaxation, a slow stirring phase lasting 30–40 minutes, before being fed into a centrifuge, which separates the oil from water and solid matter.

The extracted oil is subsequently left to settle in steel tanks for four to six weeks, a considerably longer period than the stirring phase, and is then filtered to eliminate any remaining particles. Once clarified, it is sealed in dark glass bottles. Meanwhile, the pulp left over from production is dried and burned as fuel, ensuring that the by-product is put to good use.
samples.why: Skilful overview highlighting start, product and by-product · figures used selectively for comparison · precise technical vocabulary · wide range of passive and participle structures · no noticeable errors.
